label: salt-in strategy
definition: A halophilic osmoadaptation process in which a microorganism balances external osmotic pressure by accumulating molar concentrations of inorganic ions (chiefly potassium and chloride) in the cytoplasm, rather than synthesizing organic compatible solutes.
observations: causal-graph mechanism node; parent METPO:1000059 (phenotype) is a generic fallback — maintainers may prefer an osmoadaptation/stress-response process parent
traits_addressed: covers 5 causal-graph edges across extremely_halophilic / halophilic / nacl_optimum_high (enables halophily, mitigates osmotic stress, uses K+)

label: reductive genome evolution
definition: An evolutionary process in which a microbial lineage undergoes progressive genome-size reduction through gene loss, typically under obligate host association or low effective population size.
observations: causal-graph mechanism node; parent METPO:1000059 (phenotype) is a generic fallback — maintainers may prefer a genome-evolution process parent
traits_addressed: covers 3 causal-graph edges across genome_size / genome_streamlining / endosymbiosis (caused by endosymbiosis & small effective population size; causes genome reduction)
